svg.text: for all integers x and y : x + y is odd ⇒ x ≠ y
x = y ⇒ x + y is even
a “≠” conclusion is hard to attack head-on; flipping turns it into an equation you can substitute with
x = y ⇒ x + y = x + x = 2x ⇒ x + y is even ■
the only fact used is that 2x is an even integer whenever x is an integer
Each cell is a pair (x, y).
x ≠ y but x + y even.
THE CONCLUSION IS MUCH WEAKER THAN WHAT IS TRUE
x + y odd ⇒ x − y odd ⇒ x and y have opposite parity ⇒ x ≠ y
only the last arrow is one-way, and it is the one the problem asks for — the theorem throws information away
1 + 1 + 1 = 3 is odd, yet all three are equal. For n copies of x the sum is nx, which can be odd only when n is odd —
so “odd sum forces them not all equal” is a theorem exactly for even n. Checked for n up to 7.
